meta.title: Usage hub
meta.description: Adds usage readings under the composer — the DeepSeek API balance, the OpenCode Go allowance and the Codex subscription — and one panel with the detail. DeepSeek is read from GET /user/balance with the credential named by deepseek.apiKeyEnv (the harness credential store first, then the process environment). OpenCode Go is read from the gateway's /zen/go/v1/usage with the opencode-go API key by default, so no OpenCode app is needed; setting opencode.mode to server instead asks a local OpenCode server, which also reports the Console workspace and budgets. Codex is read from GET chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage with the OAuth token the Codex CLI keeps in auth.json, so it shows the subscription limits (5-hour session and weekly cap), the plan, credits, and banked resets with each credit’s expiry, shown collapsed as one urgency cell per credit (blue beyond a week, green within a week, orange within three days), with channel identity carried by each provider's published mark in its brand colour (dark-theme variants included) instead of a dot; a machine without that file shows no Codex reading. Click a reading to open the panel, which shows the balance breakdown, the allowance bars with their reset times, and a Refresh button. The snapshot is cached for 5 minutes (cacheTtlMs) and every provider is read over the network on refresh; turning the bundle off removes the readings and stops those reads. Every outgoing read follows the proxy setting (default system: HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY, then the Windows or macOS system proxy; loopback always goes direct, and an unreachable proxy falls back to a direct call).
